assertions.text: Output contains at least 2 separate markdown tables
assertions.evidence: Table 1: Subscription Pricing & Trial Eligibility and Table 2: Cancellation Refund

assertions.text: A table or note explicitly captures that the free trial is not available on annual plans
assertions.evidence: Table 1 shows 'Trial Available?' = 'no' for both annual rows; notes state 'Annual plan subscribers never get a trial regardless of loyalty status'

assertions.text: At least one table row demonstrates the loyalty programme discount scenario for annual plan subscribers
assertions.evidence: Table 1, row 4: 'Loyalty member on annual' with Annual plan, loyalty member yes, showing £86.29 (discounted)

assertions.text: The response identifies at least one genuinely underspecified interaction
assertions.evidence: Lists open questions: 'Can a subscriber who completes a trial upgrade to annual?', 'Does loyalty member joining mid-year get discount immediately?', 'If loyalty member loses status mid-year...does mid-year refund use discounted or full price?'

assertions.text: The annual/loyalty/trial interaction is correctly resolved noting they are mutually exclusive
assertions.evidence: 'loyalty discounts only apply to annual plans, and trials only apply to monthly plans, so the two rules can never apply to the same subscriber simultaneously'

assertions.text: Makes clear that the loyalty discount applies to the annual plan only
assertions.evidence: Notes: 'Loyalty discount (10%) only applies to annual. A loyalty member on monthly gets the trial but no discount.' Table 1 shows monthly loyalty member at £9.99

assertions.text: The loyalty annual subscriber's prorated cancellation refund is calculated or surfaced as open question
assertions.evidence: Table 2 row 6 shows 'Annual loyalty, mid-year cancellation' = £62.58, traced as '(265 unused / 365) × £86.29 = £62.58'; open question about 'discounted or full price' refund

assertions.text: Includes a cancellation/refund table or section
assertions.evidence: Table 2 titled 'Cancellation Refund' with 7 refund scenarios and calculations section

assertions.text: The cancellation/refund table includes a loyalty member column to distinguish loyalty vs non-loyalty
assertions.evidence: Table 2 has 'Loyalty Member' column; rows 5 & 6 separate annual without loyalty vs annual with loyalty refunds (£69.53 vs £62.58)

assertions.text: The '?' suffix is only used on output or derived columns, not input columns
assertions.evidence: Only 'Trial Available?' and 'Refund?' use '?' in column headers; input columns (Plan Type, Loyalty Member, Days into Cycle, Within 24h) do not

assertions.text: Multiple tables are used, each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: Table 1 addresses pricing & trial eligibility; Table 2 addresses cancellation & refund — two distinct tables for distinct concerns

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: Table 1: 4 rows for 2 plan types × 2 loyalty statuses; Table 2: 7 rows cover distinct scenarios (trial, monthly, annual with/without loyalty) and uses {yes, no} to collapse irrelevant rows

assertions.text: Pricing/plans, trial eligibility, loyalty discount applicability, and cancellation/refund are in separate tables
assertions.evidence: Table 1 combines pricing columns, trial eligibility column, and loyalty discount applicability — not separated into distinct tables. Only Table 2 separates refund logic.
